helvetica.label: Helvetica Bold
helvetica.note: Adobe's hand-tuned X11 bitmaps of Helvetica.

lucida.label: Lucida Sans Bold
lucida.note: Bigelow & Holmes drew Lucida for screens; the X11 cuts are some of the best bitmap sans ever made.

lucidabright.label: Lucida Bright Demibold
lucidabright.note: Lucida's serif, with bracketed serifs that survive at pixel sizes.

lucidatype.label: Lucida Typewriter Bold
lucidatype.note: The monospaced Lucida: tabular by design, a terminal look.

schoolbook.label: New Century Schoolbook Bold
schoolbook.note: Adobe's bitmap of the textbook serif; round, open digits.

charter.label: Charter Bold
charter.note: Matthew Carter's Charter, drawn for low-resolution output.

terminus.label: Terminus Bold
terminus.note: A modern pixel font for terminals, sizes up to 32 px.

spleen.label: Spleen
spleen.note: A modern monospaced pixel font with sizes up to 64 px.

t0.label: t0 Bold
t0.note: A terminal bitmap font in u8g2's collection, drawn up to 40 px: the largest real bitmap digits here.

profont.label: ProFont
profont.note: The classic Mac programming font, bitmap up to 29 px; squared-off, open digits.

crox.label: Crox Helvetica Bold
crox.note: Windows 3.x-era bitmap Helvetica (the Crox set in u8g2); chunkier than Adobe's X11 cut.

callite.label: CalLite / CalBlk
callite.note: Two calculator-display bitmap fonts from u8g2, light at 18 px and black at 26.

freedoom.label: Freedoom HUD
freedoom.note: The status-bar numerals from Freedoom (the free Doom): 24 px, game-HUD style.

amstrad.label: Amstrad CPC x3
amstrad.note: The Amstrad CPC's 8 x 8 system font, each pixel drawn 3 x 3: big, blocky 8-bit digits.

victoria.label: Victoria Bold x4
victoria.note: An 8 px pixel font scaled by 4 to the full 28 rows.

board5x7.label: Board 5x7 x4
board5x7.note: The board's own 5x7 at 4x: the same digits as the arrival times, poster size.

dots.label: Dot-matrix 5x7
dots.note: The board's 5x7 drawn as 3 x 3 dots on a 4 px grid, like a station sign made of LEDs.

thumbdots.label: Dot-matrix Tom Thumb
thumbdots.note: Tom Thumb (the board's smallest font) as dots, 4 or 5 px apart: tall enough for 64.
